catalyst_text: FDA cleared IND for PKU gene editing program
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA cleared the investigational new drug application for a base editing therapy targeting phenylketonuria. This regulatory acceptance enables initiation of clinical testing and marks a significant step toward evaluating a potential one-time treatment for PKU.
catalyst_text_evidence: CAMBRIDGE, Mass., 2026-06-18 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Beam Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:BEAM)... announced that the United States (U.S.) Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the investigational new drug (IND) application for BEAM-304 for the treatment of phenylketonuria (PKU).

catalyst_text: Presented positive additional Phase 1/2 data at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: Additional Phase 1/2 clinical data in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency were presented at the ATS International Conference, building on topline results reported earlier in 2026. The update included detailed safety, durability of efficacy, and reductions in human neutrophil elastase activity, a direct measure of AAT function, supporting potential disease-modifying benefit.
catalyst_text_evidence: The presentation was given by Amy Simon, M.D., chief medical officer of Beam, at the American Thoracic Society (ATS) International Conference being held in Orlando, Fla. Dr. Simon's presentation at ATS features additional data for the single-dose cohorts from the same data cutoff, including detailed safety results, efficacy durability and reduction in human neutrophil elastase activity (a direct measure of AAT function) post-BEAM-302 treatment. Dr. Simon's presentation is available on the "Presentations and Publications" section of Beam's website at beamtx.com.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1/2 safety and efficacy data
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated results from an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency showed durable increases in total and functional AAT, high corrected M-AAT proportions, and strong reductions in toxic Z-AAT. Safety was generally well tolerated with single doses up to 75 mg and supported selection of 60 mg as the optimal biological dose. The dataset spans patients with lung disease and those with liver involvement, reinforcing clinical proof of mechanism.
catalyst_text_evidence: Beam Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:BEAM)... today announced updated safety and efficacy data from the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial of BEAM-302 and the selection of 60 mg as the optimal biological dose to advance into pivotal development to support potential accelerated approval. As of the 2026-02-10 data cutoff date, 29 patients have been treated with BEAM-302 in Part A (15 mg, n=3; 30 mg, n=3; 60 mg, n=6; 75 mg, n=9; 2x 60 mg, n=3) and Part B (30 mg, n=3; 60 mg, n=2) and followed for up to 18 months. Data from 26 patients treated with single-dose BEAM-302 support a well-tolerated safety profile up to 75 mg that is consistent across Part A and Part B. After treatment with a single dose of BEAM-302 in Part A, the steady-state circulating total AAT mean (LC-MS) was 16.1 µM in the 60 mg cohort (follow-up ranging from 5-12 months) and 14.4 µM in the 75 mg cohort (follow-up ranging from 2-9 months). Mutant Z-AAT was durably and significantly reduced after treatment with BEAM-302. The steady-state mean reduction in Z-AAT was 84% in the 60 mg cohort and 79% in the 75 mg cohort.

catalyst_text: Reported positive early phase SCD data at ASH
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported updated safety and efficacy results from the Phase 1/2 BEACON trial in sickle cell disease with severe vaso-occlusive crises. Data showed high HbF induction, reduced HbS, resolution of anemia, rapid engraftment, and no severe VOCs, supporting durable clinical benefit and feasibility of the approach.
catalyst_text_evidence: Beam Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:BEAM), a biotechnology company developing precision genetic medicines through base editing, today announced new safety and efficacy data from its BEACON Phase 1/2 clinical trial of ristoglogene autogetemcel (risto-cel), formerly known as BEAM-101, an investigational genetically modified ex vivo base editing cell therapy, in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) with severe vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs). Patients achieved mean HbF levels above 60% and a mean durable reduction in corresponding HbS below 40%. No patients experienced any investigator-reported severe VOCs post-engraftment. Total Hb levels increased rapidly with all patients experiencing resolution of anemia after elimination of the transfused blood.
